scope: Neutral isolated water; equilibrium geometry with a separately labelled gas-phase ground-vibrational dipole reference

geometry.coordinateMethod: Constructed from the reported equilibrium bond length and angle: O at origin, H at [±r sin(theta/2), r cos(theta/2), 0]. The construction preserves the two scalar values; it adds numerical precision rather than experimental precision.

dipole.physicalVectorConvention: Electric dipole vector points from negative to positive charge; here from the oxygen side toward the hydrogen midpoint along the angle bisector.
dipole.chemicalArrowConvention: An explicitly labelled crossed-tail chemical polarity arrow points toward oxygen; the positive tail is on the hydrogen side.

catalogReference.meaning: Approximate effective or steric probe diameter used as a catalogue scale convention. It is not a unique gas-phase envelope width, bond length or atom diameter.
catalogReference.evidenceLocation: PDF page 13 of 21, journal page 14875: 2.75 Å diameter surface-accessibility probe
catalogReference.measurementRule: Keep this approximate reference distinct from a dimension measured across a displayed van der Waals envelope. If geometry is rescaled to a unit-wide illustration, describe atom radii as illustrative and show the equilibrium measurements separately.

vanDerWaalsOption.name: Bondi van der Waals radii
vanDerWaalsOption.model: Union of overlapping atom spheres at the same equilibrium centers; atom radii model typical contact sizes.
vanDerWaalsOption.limit: The sphere surface is a contact-size approximation. It does not represent an observed hard boundary or a computed electron-density isosurface. H radius 1.20 Å specifically selects Bondi; other contact-radius conventions use 1.10 Å.

inspectionStops.label: Oxygen
inspectionStops.copy: One oxygen atom sits at the vertex of the molecule. Red is the display convention for oxygen; the ball marks an atom site.

inspectionStops.label: Two hydrogens
inspectionStops.nativeGeometry: Visible surface of one hydrogen atom ball; selection may highlight both
inspectionStops.copy: The two equivalent hydrogen atoms complete H₂O. Their centers are about 1.514 Å apart in this equilibrium geometry.

inspectionStops.label: O–H bond
inspectionStops.nativeGeometry: Exposed connector between oxygen and hydrogen display balls
inspectionStops.copy: Each O–H bond is about 0.958 Å long. Connector thickness shows connectivity and is chosen for readability.

inspectionStops.label: 104.5° bend
inspectionStops.nativeGeometry: Pickable angle guide arc clear of the oxygen ball
inspectionStops.copy: The equilibrium H–O–H angle is about 104.5°. This planar bent arrangement makes the two bond polarities reinforce along the bisector.

inspectionStops.label: Polarity toward oxygen
inspectionStops.nativeGeometry: Pickable crossed-tail chemical polarity arrow toward oxygen, clear of atom surfaces
inspectionStops.copy: The chemical polarity arrow points toward the relatively negative oxygen side. The electric dipole vector uses the opposite direction. Isolated water has a gas-phase ground-vibrational dipole magnitude of about 1.855 D. Partial charge labels show polarity; their numerical values depend on the model.

visualizationLimits: Atom balls, bond cylinders, colors, gloss and guide thickness are display choices. Ball-and-stick centers preserve the reference geometry.
A neutral water molecule has total charge zero even though its charge distribution is polar. Do not present qualitative partial charge labels as ions or measured numerical atomic charges.
Keep equilibrium atom centers rigid during inspection. Any future vibration animation needs its own labelled mode and amplitude/time conventions.
The static display omits electrons and nuclear structure. Do not add orbital trajectories, moving electron beads, or synthetic density clouds presented as experimental quantum structure.
An isolated water molecule has no intermolecular hydrogen bond. Dashed links to neighbors require a separately described multi-molecule arrangement.

The ground-vibrational dipole reference and equilibrium geometry are separate measured or inferred reference quantities; do not claim that a classical three-charge cartoon derives the measured dipole.
scopeOfFiles: Scratch-only research and numeric contract; no repository changes or runtime dependency
